## Tutorials

The PERIOD_ADD() function adds a specified number of months to a period.

The PERIOD_ADD() function will return the result formatted as YYYYMM.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT PERIOD_ADD(201703, 5);

---

PERIOD_ADD(
period
,
number
)

---

SELECT PERIOD_ADD(201703, 15);

---

SELECT PERIOD_ADD(201703, -2);
```

## Tutorials

The PERIOD_DIFF() function returns the difference between two 
periods. The result will be in months.

Note:period1andperiod2should be in the 
same format.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT PERIOD_DIFF(201710, 201703);

---

PERIOD_DIFF(
period1
,
period2
)

---

SELECT PERIOD_DIFF(201703, 201803);

---

SELECT PERIOD_DIFF(1703, 1612);
```

## Tutorials

The QUARTER() function returns the quarter of the year for a given date value (a number from 1 to 
4).

### Code Examples

```
SELECT QUARTER("2017-06-15");

---

QUARTER(
date
)

---

SELECT QUARTER("2017-01-01 09:34:21");

---

SELECT QUARTER(CURDATE());
```

## Tutorials

The SECOND() function returns the seconds part of a time/datetime (from 0 to 59).

### Code Examples

```
SELECT SECOND("2017-06-20 09:34:00.000023");

---

SECOND(
datetime
)

---

SELECT SECOND("23:59:59");
```

## Tutorials

The SEC_TO_TIME() function returns a time value (in format HH:MM:SS) based on 
the specified seconds.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT SEC_TO_TIME(1);

---

SEC_TO_TIME(
seconds
)

---

SELECT SEC_TO_TIME(-6897);
```

---
